final_answer:
All three measures are pairwise equivalent.

For one coordinate with base law \(\nu(X=1)=q\), \(\mu(X=1)=p\), \(\lambda(X=1)=r\), the joint Mellin factor is
\[
p^s r^t q^{1-s-t}+(1-p)^s(1-r)^t(1-q)^{1-s-t}.
\]
Thus
\[
M(s,t)=\prod_{k\ge3} A_k(s)B_k(t)C_k(s+t),
\]
where
\[
A_k(s)=a_k^s b_k^{1-s}+(1-a_k)^s(1-b_k)^{1-s},
\]
\[
B_k(t)=d_k^t c_k^{1-t}+(1-d_k)^t(1-c_k)^{1-t},
\]
\[
C_k(u)=e_k^u d_k^{1-u}+(1-e_k)^u(1-d_k)^{1-u},\qquad u=s+t.
\]

The critical terms are
\[
a_k^s b_k^{1-s}=k^{-4+2s}(\log k)^{-2s},
\]
\[
d_k^t c_k^{1-t}=k^{-5+3t},
\]
\[
e_k^u d_k^{1-u}=k^{-2-2u}.
\]
The remaining zero-coordinate terms differ from \(1\) only by summable corrections unless these displayed terms force divergence.

Therefore
\[
\mathcal D
=\{(s,t)\in\mathbb R^2:s\le\tfrac32,\ t<\tfrac43,\ s+t>-\tfrac12\}.
\]

Boundary behavior:

- \(s=\frac32\) is included, provided \(t<\frac43\) and \(t>-2\), because
\[
k^{-4+2s}(\log k)^{-2s}=k^{-1}(\log k)^{-3}
\]
is summable.
- \(t=\frac43\) is excluded, because \(k^{-5+3t}=k^{-1}\) diverges.
- \(s+t=-\frac12\) is excluded, because \(k^{-2-2(s+t)}=k^{-1}\) diverges.

The maximal open tube domain for holomorphic product convergence is
\[
\boxed{
\{(z,w)\in\mathbb C^2:\operatorname{Re}z<\tfrac32,\ 
\operatorname{Re}w<\tfrac43,\ 
\operatorname{Re}(z+w)>-\tfrac12\}.
}
\]

The one-variable integrability ranges are:
\[
\mathcal P_Z=\{p>0:M(p,0)<\infty\}=(0,\tfrac32],
\]
\[
\mathcal P_W=\{p>0:M(0,p)<\infty\}=(0,\tfrac43),
\]
\[
\mathcal R_\mu
=\{p>0:M(1-p,0)<\infty\}=(0,\tfrac32),
\]
\[
\mathcal R_\lambda
=\{p>0:M(0,1-p)<\infty\}=(0,\tfrac32).
\]

Also
\[
Z^{-1}W^{-1}\in L^p(\nu)
\iff M(-p,-p)<\infty
\iff -2p>-\frac12,
\]
so exactly
\[
\boxed{0<p<\frac14.}
\]

Final tuple:
\[
\boxed{
\left(
\{(s,t):s\le\tfrac32,\ t<\tfrac43,\ s+t>-\tfrac12\},
\ (0,\tfrac32],
\ (0,\tfrac43),
\ (0,\tfrac32),
\ (0,\tfrac32)
\right).
}
\]
